title: SNL’s skit Sister captures the quiet agony of caregiving for women: ‘I’ve never felt seen like that’
summary_full:
The viral satirization of the caregiving burden left to women and daughters hit home for many viewersThe Saturday Night Live sketch, titled Sister quickly went viral this week for its satirization of the burden that women and daughters face to take care of aging family members. In the parody commercial, comedian John Mulaney touts the benefit of “Sister”, who he describes as “a live-in 24/7 elder care provider that is completely free, and also your sister” .
 
 
 “Now I don’t have to worry about dad getting the care and attention he needs because my sister will do it, and I can get back to my life, and the stuff I like to do,” Mulaney says, as the sister, played by cast member Jane Wickline, gives their father’s medication to him.The sketch, which amassed over seven million views on YouTube in less than a week since it aired, has received thousands of responses and comments about its accuracy.
 
 
 “This is one of the MOST wicked and spot on SNL sketches ever written,” wrote one commenter on YouTube. Another posted: “As a hospice nurse this definitely tracks. I deal 90% of the time with adult daughters, and if there is no daughter, it is the daughter in law.”
 
 
 “This is so real it almost gave me a stroke from rage,” added another viewer. Continue reading...
